newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Midnight marks Hong Kong's red-letter handover.
newsitem.headline: Midnight marks Hong Kong's red-letter handover.

text.p: At the stroke of midnight on Monday, Hong Kong will pass from British crown colony to a part of China, ending a 156-year interlude.

Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, will preside over the ceremony returning Britain's last major colony to China -- exactly half a century after his great uncle Lord Mountbattan presided over Indian independence and the beginning of the end of the British empire.
China's President Jiang Zemin will preside over the resumption of sovereignty of the fiercely capitalist community of 6.4 million people.
The ceremony will begin at 11.30 p.m. (1530 GMT) when the audience and principal officials will be in place.
After an honour guard salute 10 minutes before midnight, Prince Charles will give his farewell speech.
Three members each from the British and Chinese armed forces will move onto the stage.
The Chinese party will present the Chinese flag to the Chinese principal officials. The British flag party will salute British officials.
Six Hong Kong police officers will then move to the stage. Three will wear the colonial uniforms of the Royal Hong Kong Police.

The other three, in the new uniforms of Hong Kong's post-colonial force, will carry the flag of the Hong Kong Special Adminstrative Region (SAR), which comes into effect at midnight, and will present it to the Chinese principals.
Shortly before midnight, the Chinese and Hong Kong SAR flags will be clipped to the poles and the notes of Britain's National Anthem, God Save the Queen, will sound out.
As the notes die away, the British Union flag and the flag of Hong Kong will be slowly lowered.
At midnight, according to th clock at Hong Kong's Royal Observatory, Hong Kong becomes a part of China.
After midnight, the Chinese National anthem will ring out and the Chinese and Hong Kong SAR flags will be raised.
The ceremony will conclude with a speech by a senior Chinese leader.
